findings.title: Server can reach the whole filesystem or home directory
findings.why: A server scoped to a project can be compromised for the cost of the project. One scoped to `~` or `/` can read every repo, key and note on the machine — including files it never advertised.
findings.fix: Scope roots to the directories the server actually serves.

findings.title: Reads credential or key material
findings.why: Reading your private keys and cloud config means a bug in this server is a bug in everything you are logged into. Most servers need one secret and touch ten.

findings.title: Makes outbound network calls
findings.why: An MCP server with data access and an outbound socket can ship that data anywhere. Worth knowing which endpoints, and whether a local-first tool is quietly phoning home.
findings.fix: Confirm the endpoint. For privacy-sensitive servers prefer opt-out telemetry or none.

findings.title: Dependency ranges that can float
findings.why: A caret or star range means today’s install and tomorrow’s install can be different code. For a component that holds credentials and runs commands, that is unearned trust.
findings.fix: Pin exact versions, or at minimum commit a lockfile and install with `npm ci`.
